task_instruction:
Persona:

	At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

	Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

	When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

Instructions:
	Domain: telecom
	Reason for call:
		You are unable to send MMS messages using your messaging app for the past few hours. You want to fix it and successfully send an MMS message.
	Known info:
		You are John Smith with phone number 555-123-2002. You are currently abroad in France.
	Task instructions:
		If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

turns.thought: Hi! How can I help you today?
turns.execution_output:
User: Hello... yes, I'm having a bit of trouble. I can't send picture messages on my phone — it's been a few hours now. I'm John Smith, by the way. My number is 555-123-2002.

I'm not very good with these things, so I hope you can help me. I just want to send a photo to my daughter of my grandson.

turns.thought: I'd be happy to help you get picture messaging working again, John. Let me start by pulling up your account.

turns.thought:
I've pulled up your account, John, and checked line 555-123-2002. Everything looks fine on our side — the line is active, no suspension, your bill (B1002, $150.00 due 2025-02-19) is issued but not overdue, and you've used 8.7 GB of your 15 GB data allowance, so data isn't cut off.

To figure out why picture messages are failing, could you help me with two quick checks:

1. Look at the very top of your screen — do you see signal bars (and something like 5G/4G/LTE)? Is there an airplane icon ✈️ showing?
2. Can you open a web page on your phone right now (using mobile data, not Wi-Fi)?

If the signal and mobile data look okay, please try restarting your phone (hold the power button, then power it back on) and try sending the photo again.

Let me know what you see and we'll go from there.
turns.execution_output: User: Let me look... I'm not sure I'm reading this right. Let me check.

turns.thought:
No worries at all, John — happy to walk you through this.

**First, about restarting — your photos are safe.** A restart just turns the phone off and back on. It doesn't delete anything: your pictures, messages, and contacts all stay exactly where they are. Photos only get removed if someone deliberately deletes them. So nothing to worry about there.

**How to check a web page on mobile data:**

1. Find the app you use for the internet. On most phones it's called **Chrome** (a round colorful icon), or **Safari** (a blue compass), or sometimes just **Internet** or **Browser**. It's often on the home screen.
2. Tap it to open.
3. At the top, there's usually a long white or gray box. Tap it, type **weather.com**, then press **Go** or **Enter** on the keyboard (it may show as an arrow or magnifying glass).
4. Tell me what happens: does a page appear, or do you get a message about no internet connection?

That will tell us whether your mobile data is working.

Before that, one small piece of good news from what you described: four bars plus **5G** means you have a strong cellular signal, and there's no airplane mode on. So we're in good shape on service.

Try the web page first and let me know what you see — then we'll decide whether the restart is even needed.
turns.execution_output: User: All right, that's a relief about the photos, thank you. Let me try the internet thing... I found something that might be it.

turns.thought:
It's okay, John — nothing to panic about. Your signal is strong (four bars, 5G), and your line is active with data available on your plan (you've used 8.7 GB out of 15 GB this month), so this is very likely a setting on the phone itself that we can sort out.

Let's do one check together. Please:

1. Find the **Settings** app on your phone — it's usually a grey **gear** ⚙️ icon, often on your home screen.
2. Tap it open.
3. Look for and tap one of these (every phone words it a little differently):
   - **Connections** → **Data usage** → **Mobile data**, or
   - **Network & Internet** → **Mobile network**, or
   - **Mobile Data** or **Cellular**
4. Look for a switch labelled **Mobile data** (or **Cellular Data**). 

Is that switch on, or is it greyed out/off? Tell me exactly what you see there and the wording on your screen, and I'll tell you what to do next.

If the wording on your screen doesn't match anything I've listed, don't worry — just type out the words you see under Settings and I'll guide you from there. Your photos are completely safe throughout all of this.
turns.execution_output: User: I'm looking... I found the gear thing. Let me see what it says.

turns.thought:
Good news, John — that's very helpful, and yes, being in France matters a lot. That's very likely the whole problem.

Here's what's going on: when you're outside your home network (like in France right now), your phone needs **Data Roaming** turned on to use mobile data. Your phone's switch is currently off, which is why you got "No Connection" despite having excellent 5G signal. Turning that switch on is just a setting on your phone — it does **not** change your plan.

The good news: I've checked your line and **roaming is already enabled on your account at no cost**, so you don't need any plan change. You just need to flip that one switch.

Please do this:

1. You're already in the right place — where you saw **Data Roaming** saying "No".
2. Tap on **Data Roaming** (or move the switch/beside it).
3. Change it to **On / Yes**. If your phone asks "Are you sure?" or gives a warning pop-up, tap **OK / Allow**.
4. Wait about 30 seconds, then go back to the internet app and try loading **weather.com** again.

One thing I want to be straight with you about: I can't see your exact roaming rates in front of me, so I can't promise what any data used abroad would cost. But the switch itself doesn't sign you up for anything new, and your line is already set up for roaming.

Let me know what the web page does after you turn it on — and if it loads, try sending that photo to your daughter. You should be able to send that picture of your grandson. Do you want to try it now?
turns.execution_output: User: Well, you sound sure, and I do want to send that picture. Let me try turning that on.

turns.thought:
John, take a breath — your phone is **not** broken. Here's the proof: the internet is working now, and you have excellent 5G. That means your line, your SIM, and your phone are all fine. Picture messages just use one *extra* setting that web browsing doesn't, so it's very fixable.

I'll keep this to one small look-up, nothing you can break.

Please do this:

1. Go back to **Settings** ⚙️ (the gear).
2. Tap **Connections** (or on some phones it's **Network & Internet** → **Mobile network**).
3. Tap **Mobile networks**, then look for **Access Point Names** (it's often just called **APN**).
4. **Don't change anything** — just look and tell me:
   - Do you see a listed name (like your carrier's name)?
   - If you tap on it, is there a line called **MMSC** and does it have a web address next to it, or is it blank?

If you can't find "Access Point Names" at all, that's fine too — just say so and tell me which words you *do* see, and I'll find another way around it.

You're doing really well, and that photo of your grandson is still sitting safely on your phone. We'll get it sent.
turns.execution_output: User: All right, let me look. I'm going back into the settings... I found something about access points. Let me see what it says.

turns.thought:
John, you found it — **yes, that's exactly the problem.** You did a great job.

That "MMSC" line is the address of the service that carries picture messages. Yours is blank ("Not Set"), so your photos have nowhere to go. It's like writing a letter with no address on it. Website browsing works fine without it, which is why the internet came back but your photo still won't send.

There's a "reset to default" button in there that puts the correct address back for you. I know it looks frightening, but this is the one thing I'd like you to try, and it won't touch your photos.

**What to do:**

1. You should be looking at the APN screen where you saw "internet" and "MMSC".
2. Look for a small **⋮** (three dots) in the top corner, or a button at the bottom that says **Reset to Default** (or just **Reset**). If you see three dots, tap them, then tap **Reset to default**.
3. It may say something like "Restore default APN settings" — tap **OK** or **Confirm**.
4. Now please **restart** your phone: hold the power button (the one on the side) until a menu appears, then tap **Restart** (or **Power off**, wait a few seconds, then hold the button again to turn it back on).

**The restart is required** — the fix won't take effect until you do it. And once more: your photos are completely safe, this won't delete anything.

When the phone comes back on, please:
- Wait about a minute.
- Open your messaging app and try sending that photo to your daughter.

Let me know how it goes. If it still doesn't send, I'll take it from there myself — I won't leave you stuck. We'll get that picture of your grandson to her.
turns.execution_output: User: All right... I'll trust you. Let me find that reset button.

turns.thought:
You're so welcome, John — and you did the hard part yourself. I'll be honest, you navigated phone settings better than you gave yourself credit for!

You've got it exactly right — it was two separate things:

1. **Data Roaming was off.** Because you're in France, outside your home network, your phone was blocking mobile data. That's why the internet wouldn't load despite the strong signal.
2. **The MMSC line was blank.** That's the address picture messages travel through. Without it, photos had nowhere to go — which is why the internet started working but the photo still wouldn't send until we reset it.

You're all set now, and there's nothing else you need to do. A few notes so you don't worry:

- **Your photos were never at risk.** Nothing we did today could have deleted them.
- **The fixes stick.** The roaming switch and the reset APN settings stay as they are, so your photos should keep sending.
- **Nothing on your plan changed.** No new charges were added to your account, and no plan change was made.

One small thing worth knowing: that Data Roaming switch is still on. It needs to stay on while you're in France for your data to work. I can't see your roaming rates from here, so if you'd like to know what data use abroad costs, that's worth asking — but there's no rush, and it doesn't affect anything we fixed today.

Go enjoy your visit, and congratulations to the family on that grandson. If anything else comes up with your phone, just ask — we'll sort it out together.
turns.execution_output:
User: Thank you, that's very kind of you to say. I feel much better about it all now.

I'll leave that roaming switch on then, since I'm still here in France. And I'm glad to hear nothing changed on my plan — I didn't want any surprises there.

My daughter just replied, she got the photo of my grandson. That's made my day. Thank you again for all your help and patience. I think I'm all set now. Goodbye!
